title: feat(security): permission-set grants and suggestions read and stamp their package column (ADR-0150 D8 R1/R3)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi99JzNTaovzGVVtXSNvcyN9Q)_

Part of #31698

Clause-②: no
Narrowing: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：权限集直授（`sys_user_permission_set`）和受众建议（`sys_audience_binding_suggestion`）改为按 `permission_set_package` 列读权限集；两张表各加一个写缝，每次写入按启动回填的同一规则盖列。
- 为什么改：ADR-0150 D8 R1/R3 的读写交接（S2 之后），是收窄一持有者拒绝的前置；本 PR 不收窄，安装门照旧。
- 风险与回滚：没有同名权限集的库授权结果逐字节不变（CONTROL pin）；null 列碰到两个以上持有者时拒绝并给出 `os migrate stored-references bind`，第一方实测 0 行。回滚即 revert。
- 先看：`packages/core/src/security/security-catalog.ts` 的精确包臂，和 `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/stored-permission-set-package-stamp.ts` 写缝。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/core exec vitest run src/security/resolve-authz-context.grant-set-by-name.test.ts`，再跑 plugin-security 的 `stored-permission-set-package-backfill.test.ts` 与 `suggested-audience-bindings.test.ts`。
- 需要你做的：无；按席位裁定，收窄（PR-2，`Fixes #31698`）等史诗席位的执行管线卡关闭后再开。

## What changes

**Reads (ADR-0150 D8 R1, R3).** The core security catalog gains one exact arm in `resolvePermissionScoped`: a reference that carries a stored package (`packageId`) reads that package's set and nothing else. A **stale** column (that package no longer serves the set: it moved to another package on an upgrade, or was renamed and its name taken) is read as a null one, so the grant follows its set as an unbound grant does on main, and the catalog says the stale (package, name) once through the plugin's logger, naming what the rule answered (review CHANGES on bf86d963, the E1 Q3 shape). This is not a substitute pick: the rule answers only when it is unique. A null column keeps today's D3 path unchanged: one holder resolves; two or more are refused with every candidate, and the refusal confers nothing. `storedPermissionSetScope(column, writer)` builds the scope; `callerPackageId` lets R3 ask from the row's own `package_id`, for a null and a stale column alike.

- R1: `resolveAuthzContext` §6b reads the grant's `permission_set_package` (added to the grant projection) and passes it to the catalog. `explain-engine` and `catalog-reference-report` read grants the same way.
- R3: `suggested-audience-bindings` resolves a suggestion by its column, else from its `package_id` (D3). Confirm/reopen on a refused name is a 409 `SuggestionStateError` that names every candidate and the exact `os migrate stored-references bind --table sys_audience_binding_suggestion --id <id> --package PACKAGE`; the everyone-anchor derivation withholds such a row with the same message.

**Writes.** `stored-permission-set-package-stamp.ts` registers one `beforeInsert` and one `beforeUpdate` hook per table (priority 40, after the grant-name refusals). It stamps the column with `permissionSetHolderOf`, the S2 backfill's rule: R1 asks with no caller, R3 from the row's `package_id`. A refused, environment-held or unheld name stays null. Before the registry seals its bare-name holders it stamps nothing and the boot backfill binds the row. A value the writer sent is replaced on insert, a system writer's included (the column is `readonly`; no writer today knows more than the name, and binding a refused name is the operator's reviewed bind, an update). With no `isSystem` read the seam adds no row to the system-context census. An update re-stamps only when the name (or R3's `package_id`) changes, so the backfill's and the reviewed bind's column-only writes stand. One seam covers every writer (plugin-auth, organizations, CLI, Setup through the data door) without editing them.

**Standing.** The column now decides which `admin_full_access` body a grant confers, so it is declared on `ADMIN_STANDING_SURFACE.sys_user_permission_set`, and `GRANT_STANDING_KEYS` in the last-administrator guard counts a payload that re-points it. Both edits are forced by the `#8734` equality gates (see Tests).

**Not changed.** The objectql install gate (`refuseSecurityCatalogNameConflicts`), the cold-boot environment check and the metadata service: a permission-set name is still held by one package per environment. `packages/spec/**` is untouched.

## Tests

- core `security-catalog.test.ts`: a nested describe, "a stored reference read by its package column" (5 pins: exact holder; a stale column reads as a null one — one holder grants, two are refused naming both, R3 from the writer, said once; ⛔ null + two holders refused naming both; null + one holder / R3 caller resolves by D3; the column ahead of a position).
- core `resolve-authz-context.grant-set-by-name.test.ts`: "[ADR-0150 D8 R1] a grant names its set's package beside its name" (5 pins: the column decides the body; ⛔ null + two holders confers nothing; a stale column still confers its one holder's set, byte-identical to the unbound grant; ⛔ a stale column with two holders confers nothing; CONTROL is byte-identical by `JSON.stringify` against a column-less run).
- plugin-security `stored-permission-set-package-backfill.test.ts`: "the write seam stamps the package column on every write that names a set" (5 pins: R1 insert; a writer's value replaced, a system writer's too; rename re-stamps, a column-only update stands; R3 asked from `package_id`; unsealed stamps nothing).
- plugin-security `suggested-audience-bindings.test.ts`: "[ADR-0150 D8 R3] a suggestion reads its set by its package column" (5 pins: column confirms; null resolves from `package_id`; a stale column confirms from `package_id`, and is a 409 naming both where that reaches two holders; ⛔ refused name is a 409 naming both candidates and the bind; derivation withholds a refused row).
- plugin-security `granted-by-writer-provenance.test.ts` (real engine, real `SecurityPlugin` and `DelegatedAdminGate`, holders sealed): "[ADR-0150 D8 R1] permission_set_package — only a system writer writes it alone" (8 pins: control stamp; a tenant-level admin and a scoped delegate, both able to edit the grant table, updating the column alone leave it as stored — the default update strip drops the value, and under `strictReadonlyWrites` the write is refused whole with `ERR_READONLY_FIELD_REJECTED`; each inserting a grant that carries the column stores the seam's answer; a system update writing it alone, the backfill's and the bind's write, lands). The seam's own insert pin is "R1: a writer's own package value is replaced by the rule's answer — a system writer's too" in `stored-permission-set-package-backfill.test.ts`.
- **Forced test edit:** core `resolve-authz-context.grant-projection.test.ts`: the expected grant read fields now include `permission_set_package` (title updated). The projection is the read list; the new column is read on purpose.
- **Forced source edits (gate-driven, outside the R1/R3 file surface):** `admin-standing-surface.ts` columns and `last-admin-guard.ts` `GRANT_STANDING_KEYS`, required by `admin-standing-surface.test.ts` ("declares exactly the columns read on sys_user_permission_set") and plugin-auth `last-admin-standing-keys.test.ts` ("every column read … is judged or excluded").

Ablations (each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, restored with `git diff HEAD` empty; core dist rebuilt and checked by `ablation-dist-preflight.mjs` where plugin suites read it):

| Mutation | Red |
|:--|:--|
| exact arm off (`const exact = undefined`) | 5 core column pins |
| refusal falls back to the first holder (dist marker present, then rebuilt and proven absent) | 6 core + 2 plugin-security (the ⛔ 409 and the withheld row) |
| insert stamp removed | 3 write-seam pins |
| update re-stamp removed | the rename pin |
| R3 reader scope dropped | 3 R3 pins |
| R1 reader scope dropped | 2 R1 pins |
| `permission_set_package` dropped from `GRANT_STANDING_KEYS` | plugin-auth standing-keys equality |
| stale-column fallback removed (returns not-found; dist marker present, then rebuilt and proven absent) | 2 core stale pins + the R3 stale pin |
| `readonly: false` on the grant's `permission_set_package` | 4 door pins (admin and delegate, strip and strict) |

## Acceptance notes

- Readings: (a) the phase-1 one-holder tests are untouched and green (objectql is not changed); (b) a single holder's bare-name behaviour is unchanged (CONTROL pin); (c) first-party `os migrate stored-references --dev` on app-crm and app-showcase: 0 findings; R1 rows are bound to `com.objectstack.plugin-security`, and showcase's one R3 row to `com.example.showcase`; (d) the install gate still refuses a second holder, so in today's environments a null column has at most one holder and the refusal arm only fires on rows the operator must bind.
- Still name-keyed after this PR, by design of the split (they move with the execution-pipeline card the epic seat files, before PR-2 narrows): `permission-evaluator` `resolvePermissionSets` (first by-name `metadataService.list('permission')` match), `ExecutionContext.permissions` (a spec `string[]`), the activation ledger `readDisabledCatalogNames`, the everyone anchor's accepted bindings, `cleanup-package-permissions` (deletes grants by name), and the plugin-auth readers `last-admin-guard` enumeration, `role-change-granted-set` and `catalog-set-in-effect`.
- Today's REST data door does not set `strictReadonlyWrites`, so a non-system update writing the column alone is a silent drop (the engine's WARN and `onFieldsDropped`), not a 400: the column is unchanged either way, as the door pins measure.
- After the narrowing, the delegated-administrator assignment gate must compare a grant by (package, name), not by name; that belongs to #31971.
- Listing stale R1/R3 rows in the S4 `os migrate stored-references` report is left as follow-up (seat ruling), not in this PR.
- `#31701` is being built in parallel; whichever lands later merges main and re-runs the gates.

## Verification

Head 4d46f6ad (commits after the first review: 2eedcedc stale fallback and door pins, 12379ff6 the warning names the rule's answer, 4d46f6ad a test typing fix the CI `tsconfig.test.json` lane caught).

- core `src/security`: 69/69 files, 1318/1318. plugin-security full suite on 2eedcedc: 255/255 files, 6133 passed, 45 skipped; on 4d46f6ad its column suites (`suggested-audience-bindings`, `granted-by-writer-provenance`, `stored-permission-set-package-backfill`, `catalog-reference-report`) 126/126. plugin-auth `src/last-admin*`: 7/7, 204/204. `tsc --noEmit` (build and `tsconfig.test.json`) clean for the touched files of core, plugin-security and plugin-auth. ESLint (`--no-inline-config`) clean on every touched file.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` (75 families, list unchanged across the heads), each run with its exit code recorded, then `--ran`: 75 accounted, 74 exit 0, 0 UNRUN, 1 NOT-MEASURED (`check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test`, exit 3: its fixture needs an unshallowed clone; the gate itself, `node scripts/check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs`, is green). The run spanned 2eedcedc→4d46f6ad, so the source-reading families (`check:system-context-census`, `check:authz-resolver`, `check:adr-symbol-anchors`, issue citations, tenant audit census, plugin teardown shape, comment mask, ADR-0087 registration, the two changeset gates) were re-run on 4d46f6ad: all exit 0.
- Every family CI runs on this PR is read from its check-runs, not re-run locally. The red runs on bf86d963, 2eedcedc and 12379ff6 are `cancelled` lanes of superseded heads, plus the one real test-typecheck error fixed in 4d46f6ad.
